The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [ADR-098](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-098.md) | philosophy-of-technology joins the topics | One topic word joins the closed vocabulary. `philosophy-of-technology` takes what technology is and what it does to those who live with it: the autonomy of technique, lock-in and practical compulsion, automation and deskilling, technical codes and the politics of artifacts, design that steers or captures its users, critical theory of technology and convivial tools. It enters because the filing of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (pull request [#489](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/489)) registered 27 works on these subjects under the nearest words, and the owner asked for the word. First applied beside the existing tags of 18 held works whose subject it is; the 27 take it once both pull requests are merged. Rejected: the nearest words (`society-and-governance`, `social-science`, `ethics`), and a broader `science-and-technology-studies`. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [ADR-099](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-099.md) v2 | A line of its own for flourishing and meaning in life, flourishing-and-meaning: what makes a life go well and be meaningful, and how arrangements and technologies widen or narrow the lives open to people | The filing of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (pull request [#489](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/489)) left A's "Convivial Modernity" programme unfiled: Wolf on meaning in life, Sen on capability and agency freedom, the "industrialization of meaning", and the claim that arrangements succeed insofar as they widen the worthwhile lives open to people. A claim needs a line, and no line holds this subject. The owner asked for one ("add the ... flourishing and meaning line"). This decision adds the line `flourishing-and-meaning`, "Flourishing and meaning in life", and says where it ends against authenticity, will-organization, organizational-normativity, transient-support, evidence-for-experience and distributed-agency. First application, under [ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md)'s test of participation: two held entries take the line beside their own, the question of what makes an experience a basic need ([QUESTION-369](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-369.md)) and the claim placing Sen's two aspects of freedom ([CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md)). That is thin, and the decision says so: the record has read little on meaning in life, and its Wolf readings are about freedom and responsibility. The intended next application is the programme of [#489](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/489). Rejected: filing the programme under the nearest line; widening authenticity; one line for the whole of [#489](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/489)'s bridge; waiting until the works are read. | Proposed |
| [ADR-100](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-100.md) | The organizational-normativity line is split in two: organizational-normativity keeps what a normative judgment needs and the wrong beyond harm; what wholes and parts owe each other, and what those who govern an arrangement others depend on owe, become the line dependence-and-domination, because those parts relate to the first two almost only through its root questions | The synthesis review of 2026-11-15 (pull request [#505](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/505)) gave organizational-normativity an account over four parts: what a normative judgment needs; the wrong beyond harm and becoming normatively less informed; what wholes and parts owe and claim; and what those who govern an arrangement others depend on owe. 93 of the line's 102 stored relations fall inside a part. Of the nine that cross, seven point at the root questions [QUESTION-128](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) and [QUESTION-129](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md), and two are [CLAIM-687](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md)'s complements. By [ADR-083](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md)'s signal the line is a candidate to split. The assistant proposed a split in two and the owner approved it ("yes on the two line split", 2026-11-15). organizational-normativity keeps the first two parts and both root questions, with a narrower blurb. A new line, `dependence-and-domination`, "Wholes, parts and dependence", takes the 29 entries of the third and fourth parts. Three of them keep organizational-normativity second, because they refine or bear on a root question ([ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md)). The accounts follow: the two parts' accounts take the new line under a new line account, and [SYNTHESIS-038](../../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) is revised over the first two. Rejected: keeping one line; a line of its own for the fourth part; a split in four; moving the parts into distributed-agency. | Proposed |
| [ADR-101](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-101.md) | A repository's documented machine interface to an open-access full text is a lawful route in its own right, and a bot check on the repository's website does not bar it; Europe PMC's REST API is the first such route | On the owner's ruling of 2026-11-17 ("Europe PMC is fine"). [ADR-074](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md) and the read-and-file skill say to stop at any bot check and never work around one. On 2026-11-15 a reader met challenges at europepmc.org and PMC for a CC BY review, then fetched the same full text from Europe PMC's documented REST API on www.ebi.ac.uk. The lead accepted the route and left it to the owner, who confirmed it. This decision says why that is not a workaround: the API is the repository's own published route for machine access to the text, not a way past the check that guards its website. It adds the route to the skill's step 5. The bar on working around a check stands. A route counts only if the repository documents it for machine access and the text it serves is open access. | Proposed |
| [ADR-102](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-102.md) | A copy its host says is published with the rights holders' permission, and a reply posted by the scholar it answers beside that scholar's own paper, count as lawful copies to read, beside the kinds already admitted | Extends [ADR-074](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md)'s list of lawful copies with two kinds, on the owner's ruling of 2026-11-18 ("both permission copies count as lawful"). (1) A copy whose host states that it is published with the permission of the rights holders (the publisher, the author, or the author's estate). (2) A reply, comment or response posted on the personal site of the scholar it answers, beside that scholar's own paper, as part of the exchange the two pieces belong to. [ADR-074](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md)'s kinds and exclusions are unchanged, and so is [ADR-053](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md)'s line between Unfetched and Unavailable. The NOTE names the copy and quotes the permission statement or says whose site it is. The first application is the readings of 2026-11-18: Strawson's "Freedom and Resentment", and Scanlon's "Reply to Leif Wenar". | Proposed |
| [ADR-103](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-103.md) | A line rightful-power is added beside dependence-and-domination and organizational-normativity, without moving any entry out of them: its root questions carry it first, and an entry carries it when it takes part in its argument | On the owner's decision of 2026-11-18 ("go ahead with the line, first-line option"), the closed lines vocabulary gains rightful-power, "Rightful power: restriction, answerability and rights", for the argument filed from the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse". Unlike [ADR-100](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-100.md)'s split, it is additive: no entry loses a line. Its six root questions, the owner's, carry it first and keep their earlier lines after it. Every other entry carries it, after its own lines, exactly when [ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md) says so: it answers, objects to or bears on a root question, or refines one. Where an entry argued a root question without saying so, the relation was written with a reason; no entry was given the line by hand. [SYNTHESIS-100](../../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-100.md) becomes the line's account. | Proposed |
| [ADR-104](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-104.md) v2 | A work capability-restraint-relational-freedom is added for the owner's manuscript from the exchange Assess Depp Heard Abuse: a claim is a member when the manuscript or an addition offered for it states the claim's proposition or uses it as a step | At the owner's request of 2026-11-18, the closed works vocabulary gains capability-restraint-relational-freedom, "Capability, Restraint, and Relational Freedom". It is the manuscript the owner asked for at U22 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse". ChatGPT drafted it at A49 and offered additions in later turns. A claim or ARG is a member when the manuscript, or a passage that A explicitly offers for it, states the entry's proposition or uses it as a step. Membership says nothing of status ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)). The owner expected the work to be mostly a subset of the line rightful-power. On reading, it is not: 27 claims are members, and only 6 carry the line. The manuscript's question, its last sections and the later additions sit in the line. Its body relays the record's earlier claims on dependence, correction, self-binding and capability trajectories, and those keep their own lines. Rejected: counting only entries filed from the exchange; restricting the work to members of the line; counting what the provenance table cites but the text does not use; and having no work. | Proposed |
| [ADR-105](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-105.md) | Docs runs on pushes to the default branch wait for one another and are never cancelled: one concurrency group serializes view generation, so two merges minutes apart no longer race | On the default branch, every push used to get a concurrency group of its own, so two merges a few minutes apart ran docs-generate at the same time and both runs failed: the first committed views that no longer matched the sources the second merge had added, and the second could not rebase its view commit onto the first's. Main was left with stale views and a red run. Pushes now share one group, without cancellation, so their runs go one at a time. A group holds one pending run, so a third push replaces the one waiting; that is harmless because docs-generate checks out the branch, not the triggering commit. Rejected: leaving it (it recurs whenever merges cluster); cancelling in progress (a cancelled run can leave concretized codes or repairs unpushed); fixing the rebase in luria's generate action (the right long-term place, outside this repository, and already proposed there for the pull-request race). | Proposed |
| [ADR-106](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-106.md) | A work cost-structure-of-possibility is added for the owner's manuscript from the exchange Topological protection explained: a claim is a member when the manuscript or an addition offered for it states the claim's proposition or uses it as a step | At the owner's decision of 2026-11-19, the closed works vocabulary gains cost-structure-of-possibility, "The Cost Structure of Possibility". It is the manuscript the owner asked for at U19 of the exchange "Topological protection explained", which ChatGPT drafted at A43. Membership follows [ADR-104](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-104.md)'s rule: a claim or ARG is a member when A43, or a passage A explicitly offers for it, states the entry's proposition or uses it as a step; a reference-list citation alone does not count. Membership says nothing of status ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)). On reading, 20 claims are members, 8 of them Proposed: 16 on the default branch and 4 filed from the exchange itself in the same pull request. They sit mostly in the lines realizability and formal-apparatus. Rejected: counting the reference list; counting every claim that is an instance of A43's general amortization result; and having no work. | Proposed |
| [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) | A delegated reader keeps running notes in the repository, outside the record, on a branch of its own that it pushes as it reads, so the owner can see a reading in flight; the notes are removed when the reading is filed, and no downloaded text is ever committed | [ADR-068](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)'s eighth invariant had readers draft outside the repository, so a long reading showed nothing until its report came back. The owner asked on 2026-11-19 for readers' notes to be version-controlled and visible in flight, and removed when filed. The owner proposed record/workbench.d, but it is a luria journal, "dated and never rewritten" and rendered (133 entries), so a reader's transient notes would break its contract. Instead a reader writes only scratch/readers/<key>.md, outside record/, in its own worktree on a branch claude/readers/<key> with no pull request, and commits and pushes after each step. Readers still do not write to the record. The filer files from the final report and deletes the branch. Downloaded texts stay out of the repository. Changes [ADR-068](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)'s eighth invariant; the rest stands. Rejected: the workbench; readers pushing to the filing branch; the filer saving reports after the fact. | Proposed |
| [ADR-109](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-109.md) | The record keeps its research opportunities as LEADs, plans to advance a question or claim by any method, with a status for whether each is still worth following and a stage for how far it is worked out; and a question may presuppose another | The record's research opportunities were scattered: proposed-study CASEs (54, 28 of them bearing on no question), "What would answer it?" prose on 264 of 451 open questions, and proposed tests in dated notes. Nothing said which were still wanted, how far each was worked out, or which waited on which, and an opportunity that was not an experiment had no form at all. The owner asked on 2026-11-19 for a better way to represent this backlog, and supported dependencies among questions. A new scheme, LEAD, holds a plan to advance a question or claim: by reading, conceptual or formal work, a study, a history, or working out how a question could be advanced at all. Its status (Open, Done, Dropped, Superseded) says whether it is still worth following; a separate `stage` (idea, specified, underway) how far it is worked out. It `advances` questions and claims, may be `operationalized_in` a CASE that holds its design, and may `presuppose` a lead or a question. Questions gain `presupposes`, after THEORY's ([ADR-029](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-029.md)). Rejected: a "What would advance it?" section on every question; decision gates on claims; more fields on CASE; a backlog file outside the record. | Proposed — Amended by ADR-111 (2026-11-20): a priority and a blocked_on note, a costed stage after specified, advances widened to readings and terms, and the converse blurbs corrected. |
| [ADR-110](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-110.md) | A postmortem is due when a schema change has been used, a batch of pull requests closes, a bulk filing lands, a decision is revised soon after landing, a process incident is fixed, or the owner asks; triggers count use and sessions, not calendar time, and a starting policy expected to be superseded | The owner asked on 2026-11-20 when to write a postmortem: not for every pull request, but perhaps for batches. Six triggers, measured in use and in working sessions because the record moves at about ten pull requests, one to five hundred entries and two decisions a day: a change to luria.yaml once about 20 entries use it or at the close of the first session that used it; a batch of five or more pull requests in a session, or any stack that had to be folded; a bulk filing of more than about 50 generated entries; a decision revised within the session it landed or the next; a process incident, once fixed; the owner's request. Not routine single filings that go green first time, nor the bot's repairs. The assistant checks the triggers when a batch closes and proposes; the owner decides. Short form for batches and incidents, the full form for schema changes. The owner expects this to be superseded: it is a starting policy, to be revised as postmortems show what is worth reviewing. Rejected: a postmortem per pull request; calendar intervals; leaving it to ad hoc request. | Proposed |
| [ADR-111](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-111.md) | LEADs get a priority for triage and a blocked_on note; the stage ladder separates a specified design from a costed one; a lead may advance a reading or a term as well as a question or claim; and derived converses are stated as computed, not stored | Carries out recommendations 1 to 5 of [POSTMORTEM-002](../../../record/postmortems.d/POSTMORTEM-002.md), the review of [ADR-109](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-109.md) after the backlog audit filed 184 leads. A `priority` (high, medium, low) for triage, backfilled from the audit's ratings (59 high, 125 medium). The stage `specified` no longer needs a cost, which no source gave; a new stage `costed` holds what does; 53 leads whose design is in a CASE move from idea to specified, and one to costed. A plain `blocked_on` field says what a lead waits on that the record cannot do; two reading leads carry one. `advances` may name a THEORY (a replication that would meet its promote_when) or a TERM (the operationalization it waits on), with `advanced_by` derived on both. The blurbs of the derived converses now say they are computed for every reader and never stored, which is how luria treats a directed pair; they had said they were written by `luria link --fix`. QUESTION `presupposes` is kept, unused, until a sweep of question dependencies. Rejected: sorting the index by priority in place of line; a `blocked` status; dropping question dependencies; storing the converses. | Proposed |
| [ADR-112](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-112.md) | The record keeps postmortems as POSTMORTEMs, reviews of how a change to the record has worked out once used, which review the decisions behind the change, link the pull requests that carried it and the discussions that asked for the review, and name the decisions their recommendations prompt | On 2026-11-20 the owner asked for a postmortem of the session's changes to luria.yaml, then for a scheme to hold such reviews, related to the decisions they review, with the pull requests and the discussion linked. A new scheme, POSTMORTEM: it `reviews` one or more ADRs (converse `reviewed_by`, derived on ADR), may name the decisions its recommendations `prompted` (converse `prompted_by`), and carries `pull_requests` and `discussions` as URL lists. Statuses Draft, Accepted, Superseded. First application: [POSTMORTEM-002](../../../record/postmortems.d/POSTMORTEM-002.md), on [ADR-106](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-106.md), [ADR-107](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-107.md) and [ADR-109](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-109.md). Rejected: a curation entry; a workbench entry; new history versions on each reviewed ADR; reviews as dated notes on the ADRs. | Proposed |
